subject.title: fix: gate Gateway message action requester provenance [AI]

question: Should OpenClaw accept the intentional `message.action` compatibility change that strips requester provenance from non-admin/write-scoped callers while preserving the trusted backend bridge?
rationale: The patch closes a requester-provenance spoofing boundary, but existing write-scoped integrations that depended on caller-supplied requester identity will observe different authorization context after upgrade.

options.title: Accept Boundary Change
options.body: Proceed after current-base validation because the patch keeps the trusted backend bridge while denying write-scoped requester spoofing.

options.title: Pause For Contract Design
options.body: Keep the PR open if maintainers want docs, a migration story, or a different permanent provenance contract before changing existing client behavior.

options.title: Close And Replace
options.body: Close this PR only if maintainers decide the compatibility break is unacceptable or needs a broader owner-authored redesign.

recommendation.title: Accept Boundary Change
recommendation.body: Proceed after current-base validation because the patch keeps the trusted backend bridge while denying write-scoped requester spoofing.

likelyOwner.reason: mcaxtr introduced and merged the Gateway-routed message-action path that defines the compatibility boundary being changed.
